title: The Full Pipeline: Genotypes to a Certified Mating Plan

what: Stage 11 – Solve for actual optimal contributions
title: The Full Pipeline: Genotypes to a Certified Mating Plan
text: select_parents_ocs() solves real Optimal Contribution Selection problem (Meuwissen 1997): much parent contribute, specific matings deliver , relatedness ceiling set target_degree (informed stage 8’s frontier). run restricted stage 5-8 shortlist (merit/G subset ga_sel$selected), full 120-individual population, output stays candidate pool stage 10’s ranking stage 13’s exact-validation comparison – OCS solving “allocate already-shortlisted set”, re-shortlisting scratch. needs optional optiSel SimpleMating packages; neither installed, usefulness -criterion ranking stage 10 stands shortlist stages 12-13 .

what: Stage 12 – Certify the plan and check its sensitivity
title: The Full Pipeline: Genotypes to a Certified Mating Plan
text: certify_mating_plan() validates complete plan family size, parent capacity, required pairs, period-specific capacity subpopulation quotas, returns every binding constraint alongside certificate. assess_decision_stability() (run – see “Sensitivity” programme operations vignette) compares certified plan threshold, model population-scenario variants.
code: plan_pairs <- if (have_ocs) ocs_res$mating_plan else mating_plan plan <- data.frame(   female = plan_pairs$parent1,   male = plan_pairs$parent2,   family_size = 20 ) plan_status <- data.frame(   id = unique(c(plan$female, plan$male)),   female_allowed = TRUE, male_allowed = TRUE, fertile = TRUE,   flowering_start = 5, flowering_end = 9 ) certificate <- certify_mating_plan(plan, plan_status, min_family_size = 20) certificate$certificate #>   feasible n_crosses total_families n_violations n_binding_constraints #> 1     TRUE        10            200            0                     0

title: Introduction to HapBlockR
text: HapBlockR detects linkage disequilibrium (LD) blocks genome-wide SNP data extends pipeline haplotype reconstruction, diversity analysis, genomic prediction feature engineering. Two LD metrics available: Standard r² – fast, kinship correction, suitable 10 M+ markers unstructured populations. Kinship-adjusted rV² – corrects relatedness-induced LD inflation, livestock, inbred lines, family-based cohorts. See LD Metrics vignette statistical detail decision table. C++/Armadillo computational core makes algorithm approximately 40x faster original Big-LD implementation typical window sizes. vignette covers complete pipeline – reading genotype data, block detection, haplotype analysis, parameter tuning – using ldx_geno example dataset (120 individuals, 230 SNPs, 3 chromosomes, 9 simulated LD blocks). Everything builds toward breeding decision: block detection defines units haplotype analysis operates , haplotype analysis turns units per-block genetic values, Section 13.5 shows first step turning ranked list candidates. full path actual selected set parents – GA-based parent selection truncation-selection baseline, family/diversity checks, forward-simulated genetic gain – see Local GEBV Crossing Decision vignette.

what: 13.6 Haplotype association testing with simpleM correction
title: Introduction to HapBlockR
text: test_block_haplotypes() uses unified Q+K mixed linear model. simpleM procedure (Gao et al. 2008, 2010, 2011) estimates effective number independent tests (Meff) eigenspectrum haplotype allele dosage correlation matrix, providing family-wise error control less conservative raw Bonferroni. fitted Q+K model accounts population structure genomic relatedness, FDR, Bonferroni simpleM options control multiplicity. statistically supported haplotype can identify segment harbouring causal gene variant, particularly effect replicates across populations. HapBlockR provides cross-population harmonisation, epistasis scans fine mapping strengthen localise biological hypothesis. Interpret association resolution tested segment; claiming specifically causal variant additionally uses positional, functional experimental evidence. estimate_diplotype_effects() now supports correction set test_block_haplotypes(). five p-value columns always present $omnibus_tests; sig_metric controls drives significant flag:
code: blues_vec <- setNames(ldx_blues$YLD, ldx_blues$id)  # EMMAX with FDR — recommended for discovery assoc_fdr <- test_block_haplotypes(   haplotypes = haps,   blues      = blues_vec,   blocks     = blocks,   n_pcs      = 0L,   sig_metric = "p_fdr",   verbose    = FALSE ) cat("Significant (FDR <= 0.05):", sum(assoc_fdr$allele_tests$significant), "\n")  # Q+K with simpleM Šidák — recommended for family-wise error control assoc_sm <- test_block_haplotypes(   haplotypes       = haps,   blues            = blues_vec,   blocks           = blocks,   n_pcs            = 3L,                 # Q+K model (used when optimize_pcs = FALSE)   sig_metric       = "p_simplem_sidak",  # simpleM Šidák correction   meff_scope       = "chromosome",       # recommended: separate Meff per chr   meff_percent_cut = 0.995,              # 99.5% variance threshold (Gao default)   verbose          = FALSE )  # Per-chromosome Meff assoc_sm$meff$trait$allele$chromosome  # All four p-value columns always present regardless of sig_metric # p_wald | p_fdr | p_simplem | p_simplem_sidak | Meff | alpha_simplem | ... head(assoc_sm$allele_tests[order(assoc_sm$allele_tests$p_wald),                             c("block_id","allele","effect","SE",                               "p_wald","p_simplem","p_simplem_sidak","Meff")], 5)  # Automatic PC selection — let the data choose n_pcs via BIC/lambda hybrid # Recommended when lambda_GC is far from 1.0 with a fixed n_pcs. assoc_opt <- test_block_haplotypes(   haplotypes       = haps,   blues            = blues_vec,   blocks           = blocks,   optimize_pcs     = TRUE,              # triggers BIC/lambda model selection   optimize_pcs_max = 10L,              # test k = 0..10   optimize_method  = "bic_lambda",     # recommended: |lambda-1| + 0.01*BIC   sig_metric       = "p_simplem_sidak",   meff_scope       = "chromosome",   plot             = TRUE,             # saves PDF plots including pca_grm.pdf   out_dir          = "results",        # and grm_scree.pdf   verbose          = TRUE )  # Inspect selection table print(assoc_opt$pc_model_selection) #  n_pcs     BIC lambda_gc  score selected #      0  1234.1     1.021 0.0210    FALSE #      1  1231.5     1.015 0.0150    FALSE #      2  1230.8     1.003 0.0033    FALSE #      3  1232.1     0.999 0.0011     TRUE   <-- selected  # Multi-trait: all traits share the same GRM assoc_mt <- test_block_haplotypes(   haplotypes = haps,   blues      = ldx_blues,   blocks     = blocks,   id_col     = "id",   blue_cols  = c("YLD", "RES"),   n_pcs      = 3L,   sig_metric = "p_simplem_sidak",   verbose    = FALSE ) dip <- estimate_diplotype_effects(   haplotypes       = haps,   blues            = blues_vec,   blocks           = blocks,   min_n_diplotype  = 3L,   sig_metric       = "p_omnibus_simplem_sidak",  # recommended   meff_percent_cut = 0.995,   verbose          = FALSE )  # All five columns always present: # p_omnibus_adj | p_omnibus_fdr | p_omnibus_simplem | p_omnibus_simplem_sidak | Meff head(dip$omnibus_tests[, c("block_id","trait","F_stat","p_omnibus",                             "p_omnibus_fdr","p_omnibus_simplem_sidak",                             "Meff","significant")], 5)  # Blocks showing overdominance (heterosis candidates) dip$dominance_table[dip$dominance_table$overdominance,                     c("block_id","allele_A","allele_B","a","d","d_over_a")]

title: Introduction to HapBlockR
text: compare_block_effects() validates whether haplotype effects one population replicate another. computes IVW meta-analytic effects, Cochran Q heterogeneity (tests whether effect sizes differ populations), ² inconsistency, direction agreement per block. Key distinction: boundary_overlap_ratio output column automatically computed block tables supply — set . boundary_overlap_warn input parameter (default 0.80) controls boundary_warning = TRUE raised output. code: # Best practice: use Pop A's block boundaries for Pop B to maximise # shared alleles and ensure haplotype strings are directly comparable. haps_B_harm <- harmonize_haplotypes(   extract_haplotypes(geno_B, snp_info, blocks_A),  # same block coordinates   reference = haps_A )  assoc_A <- test_block_haplotypes(haps_A, blues = blues_A, blocks = blocks_A,                                   sig_metric = "p_simplem_sidak") assoc_B <- test_block_haplotypes(haps_B_harm, blues = blues_B, blocks = blocks_A,                                   sig_metric = "p_simplem_sidak")  # block_match = "id" (default): match by block_id string # block_match = "position": match by genomic IoU -- use when blocks differ conc <- compare_block_effects(   assoc_A, assoc_B,   pop1_name             = "PopA",   pop2_name             = "PopB",   blocks_pop1           = blocks_A,   blocks_pop2           = blocks_B,   # Pop B own block table (may differ)   block_match           = "position", # recommended when blocks not identical   overlap_min           = 0.50,   direction_threshold   = 0.75,   boundary_overlap_warn = 0.80 )  # $concordance — one row per block: IVW effect, Q_stat, I2, replicated, ... conc$concordance[conc$concordance$replicated,                  c("block_id","n_shared_alleles","direction_agreement",                    "meta_p","Q_p","I2","replicated")]  # $shared_alleles — per-allele IVW detail head(conc$shared_alleles[, c("block_id","allele","effect_pop1","effect_pop2",                                "direction_agree","ivw_effect","ivw_SE")])  print(conc)   # summary: n blocks compared, n replicated, median I²

title: Introduction to HapBlockR
text: GWAS run outside HapBlockR, use compare_gwas_effects(). accepts either output define_qtl_regions() (recommended, auditable) raw GWAS data frames plus block tables (convenience path). Note external GWAS provides one lead SNP per block (multiple haplotype alleles), effect_correlation Cochran Q always NA. Replication judged direction agreement meta_p ≤ 0.05.
code: # Path 1: pre-mapped (recommended) # define_qtl_regions() maps each marker to its LD block and identifies # the lead SNP (smallest p-value) as the block representative. qtl_A <- define_qtl_regions(gwas_A, blocks, snp_info, p_threshold = 5e-8) qtl_B <- define_qtl_regions(gwas_B, blocks, snp_info, p_threshold = 5e-8)  conc_gwas <- compare_gwas_effects(   qtl_pop1    = qtl_A,   qtl_pop2    = qtl_B,   blocks_pop1 = blocks_A,   blocks_pop2 = blocks_B,   block_match = "position",   overlap_min = 0.50,   pop1_name   = "PopA",   pop2_name   = "PopB" )  # Path 2: raw GWAS + blocks (calls define_qtl_regions internally) # When SE is absent, it is derived from BETA and P via z-score. # Column names are flexible: use beta_col, se_col, p_col arguments. conc_raw <- compare_gwas_effects(   gwas_pop1     = gwas_A,   gwas_pop2     = gwas_B,   blocks_pop1   = blocks,   blocks_pop2   = blocks,   snp_info_pop1 = snp_info,   # snp_info_pop2 reuses this when NULL (shared panel)   pop1_name     = "PopA",   pop2_name     = "PopB",   p_threshold   = 5e-8,   beta_col      = "BETA",     # change if named differently in your GWAS output   se_col        = "SE",       # NULL or absent: derived from z-score automatically   p_col         = "P" )  # Same output class as compare_block_effects() # Extra columns: lead_marker_pop1/pop2, lead_p_pop1/pop2, #                se_derived_pop1/pop2, both_pleiotropic conc_gwas$concordance[conc_gwas$concordance$replicated, ] print(conc_gwas)

title: Introduction to HapBlockR
text: HapBlockR v0.3.1 adds three epistasis functions operate GRM-corrected REML residuals null model test_block_haplotypes(). Within-block SNP interaction scan (scan_block_epistasis): tests C(p,2) SNP pairs inside significant blocks interaction term aaij y = mu + aixi + ajxj + aaij(xixj) + e. Corrected Bonferroni simpleM Sidak within block; sig_metric controls drives significant flag. -block trans-haplotype scan (scan_block_by_block_epistasis): tests significant haplotype alleles every allele blocks. Identifies genetic background dependence haplotype resolution — form epistasis single-block single-SNP analyses detect. Single-block fine-mapping (fine_map_epistasis_block): identifies specific interacting SNP pair within block. Auto-dispatches exhaustive pairwise scan (p <= 200 SNPs) LASSO interaction terms (p > 200 SNPs). Statistical note. n=204 individuals Bonferroni correction ~300,000 within-block pairs, detection threshold approximately p < 1.7 × 10^-7 per block. Power detect pairwise SNP epistasis threshold low unless interaction effect large (|aa| > ~0.3 SD). -block trans-haplotype scan better powered haplotype dosage column aggregates multi-SNP variation, reducing effective number tests increasing signal--noise ratio per test.
code: # Within-block epistasis (restricted to significant_omnibus blocks) epi_within <- scan_block_epistasis(   assoc              = assoc,   geno_matrix        = res$geno_matrix,   snp_info           = snp_info,   blocks             = blocks,   blues              = blues_list,   haplotypes         = haps,   trait              = "BL",   sig_metric         = "p_simplem_sidak",   max_snps_per_block = 300L ) print(epi_within) epi_within$results[epi_within$results$significant, ]  # Between-block trans-haplotype epistasis epi_between <- scan_block_by_block_epistasis(   assoc      = assoc,   haplotypes = haps,   blues      = blues_list,   blocks     = blocks,   trait      = "BL" ) print(epi_between)  # Fine-map a single block # y_resid must be pre-computed from the REML null model fine <- fine_map_epistasis_block(   block_id    = "block_12_1054210_1086071",   geno_matrix = res$geno_matrix,   snp_info    = snp_info,   blocks      = blocks,   y_resid     = my_reml_residuals,   method      = "auto" ) head(fine)

title: Clique-Based LD Block Detection — CLQD
text: Partitions SNPs genomic window LD cliques. Three algorithms available via CLQmode: "Density" (default) Standard Big-LD clique scoring – edges     built full r? matrix, cliques found Bron-Kerbosch     (igraph::max_cliques), scored density = size / span.     Exact, exponential worst-case. Use checkLargest = TRUE     guard blowup dense WGS panels. "Maximal" algorithm Density scored clique     size (original Big-LD maximality criterion). "Louvain" Louvain community detection     (igraph::cluster_louvain). Polynomial time O(n log n) – never     exponential. Recommended WGS panels (>500 SNPs per window)     time CLQmode = "Density" slow. Communities returned     bin IDs matching Density output format downstream code     unaffected. "Leiden" Leiden community detection     (igraph::cluster_leiden). Stricter Louvain – produces     well-connected communities without disconnected nodes. Requires     igraph >= 1.3.0. Slightly slower Louvain higher quality     communities. Recommended Louvain resolution matters. max_bp_distance supplied (> 0), SNP pairs within physical distance r? computed (compute_r2_sparse_cpp). reduces O(p?) LD computation near-O(p) WGS panels long-range LD negligible (typically > 500 kb). Applied clique algorithm.

title: Cross-Population Haplotype Effect Concordance — compare_block_effects
text: Given two allele_tests data frames produced test_block_haplotypes two independent populations, computes per-block (optionally per-trait) statistics quantify consistently haplotype allele effects replicate across populations. Statistics computed per block: Effect correlation (\(r\)) Pearson correlation per-allele     effect sizes populations across shared alleles. Requires     least 3 shared alleles; NA otherwise. Direction agreement Proportion shared alleles     populations assign sign effect. value >= 0.75     (.e. least 3 4 alleles agree direction) considered     strong directional replication. Inverse-variance weighted (IVW) meta-analytic effect weighted     mean effect \(\hat\beta_{\mathrm{IVW}} = \sum w_i \beta_i /     \sum w_i\) \(w_i = 1/\mathrm{SE}_i^2\).  Computed separately     shared allele summarised mean per-allele IVW     estimates. IVW meta-analysis framework used     two-sample Mendelian randomisation cross-population GWAS     meta-analysis (see Borenstein et al. 2009). Cochran's Q heterogeneity statistic Tests whether effect sizes     differ significantly two populations:     \(Q = \sum w_i (\beta_i - \hat\beta_{\mathrm{IVW}})^2\).     null heterogeneity, \(Q \sim \chi^2_{n-1}\).     Significant Q (large \(Q_p\)) indicates effect sizes differ     populations - sign GxE interaction, LD structure     differences, population-specific allelic action. \(^2\) inconsistency \(^2 = 100 \times \max(0,\, (Q - df)/Q)\).     Values > 50% indicate substantial -population heterogeneity. Block boundary concordance blocks_pop1     blocks_pop2 supplied, bp overlap ratio two     populations' block definitions computed block. ratio     < 0.8 flags blocks LD structure likely differs     populations effect comparisons interpreted cautiously. Addressing two principal limitations cross-population validation: Population structure confounding: Q+K mixed model     test_block_haplotypes() already corrects within-population     structure via haplotype GRM.  Cross-population validation     inherently controls -population confounding design:     haplotype allele must associate phenotype genetically     distinct background, making false-positive carry-Pop 's     stratification implausible.  meta-analytic \(^2\) statistic     additionally flags cases effect sizes heterogeneous     shared biological mechanism unlikely. LD block boundary differences: Block boundaries can differ     populations due different historical recombination rates     ancestral haplotype structure.  boundary_overlap_ratio     column quantifies directly every block.  Low overlap (< 0.8)     means two populations carve genomic region blocks     different sizes; case haplotype allele tested 50 kb     window Pop compared allele 30 kb window Pop B     strings match well.  n_shared_alleles     column empirical consequence: low shared-allele counts     despite adequate allele frequencies populations direct     symptom block boundary mismatch.  recommended remedy - passing     Pop 's block table blocks argument     test_block_haplotypes() Pop B - eliminates issue     entirely forcing runs use identical coordinates.

what: Cross-Population GWAS Effect Concordance from External Results — compare_gwas_effects
title: Cross-Population GWAS Effect Concordance from External Results — compare_gwas_effects
text: Compares haplotype block-level association signals two populations GWAS run externally (e.g. GAPIT, TASSEL, FarmCPU, PLINK, tool) rather test_block_haplotypes. function accepts external GWAS results two ways: Pre-mapped (recommended): supply output     define_qtl_regions population. QTL table     already maps marker LD block, providing lead SNP,     effect size (BETA), p-value per block.     reliable input block assignment explicit. Raw GWAS + blocks: supply raw GWAS data frames plus block     tables; function calls define_qtl_regions internally     map markers blocks comparing. compared : External GWAS produces marker-level effects, haplotype-allele-level effects. block level population contributes one observation: lead SNP (smallest p-value block). comparison therefore analogous two-sample Mendelian randomisation - one effect estimate per exposure (block) per population, combined via IVW meta-analysis. one "allele" per block (lead SNP), several statistics differ compare_block_effects: n_shared_alleles always 1 (lead SNP concept). effect_correlation always NA (needs >= 3 alleles). direction_agreement 0 1 (sign lead SNP effect agrees     ). Q_df always 0 (one observation per population; Cochran Q     undefined two populations one allele per block). meta_p tests whether IVW combined effect differs     zero - primary replication test. Standard error derivation: Many GWAS tools report BETA P SE. SE absent, compare_gwas_effects() derives z-score: $$SE = \frac{|\beta|}{|z|},\quad z = \Phi^{-1}(P/2)$$ \(\Phi^{-1}\) standard normal quantile function. exact large-sample Wald tests (dominant GWAS framework) provides valid SE IVW weighting. Interpreting pleiotropic blocks: trait_col supplied GWAS results contain multiple traits, function compares trait trait. Blocks significant multiple traits populations (pleiotropic = TRUE QTL tables) flagged both_pleiotropic = TRUE output, identifying robust cross-population replication targets.

text: SNP \(j\) reference-allele frequency \(p_j\) (dosage mean / 2) \(q_j = 1-p_j\), dominance incidence coding $$S_{ij} = \begin{cases} -2q_j^2 & \text{dose} = 0 \\ 2p_jq_j & \text{dose} = 1 \\ -2p_j^2 & \text{dose} = 2 \end{cases}$$ \(D = SS' / \sum_j (2p_jq_j)^2\). Dosage values rounded nearest genotype class (0/1/2) coding, warning value far integer call (e.g. imputed dosage probabilities rather hard genotype calls) – allele frequencies use original, unrounded dosage less biased estimate.

text: C++ acceleration: pairwise r\(^2\) computations use package's compiled C++ kernels (Armadillo BLAS via RcppArmadillo): Random sampling: compute_r2_sparse_cpp() computes     pairs within max_dist single C++ call compact     submatrix, replacing R pair--pair loop. n_threads     forwarded enable OpenMP parallelism. Sliding window: column preparation done per window     via apply(); within-window stats::cor() used     (windows small, typically 50 SNPs). Parametric threshold: col_r2_cpp() computes     cross-chromosome r\(^2\) Armadillo BLAS. Memory-efficient backend access: GDS bigmemory backends function never loads full chromosome. Instead samples pair indices SNP positions (genotype /O), collects unique SNP indices involved, calls read_chunk() compact set. 50,000 random pairs 500,000-SNP chromosome 500 individuals, peak RAM approximately 40 MB rather 2 GB. Important: method = "rV2" memory-safe WGS scale. kinship whitening matrix requires full-genome read SNPs per-chromosome processing begins. panels millions markers can dominant memory step. Use method = "r2" LD decay estimation; reserve method = "rV2" block detection. Sampling strategies: "sliding_window" Computes r\(^2\) within moving     window window_snps SNPs, reading columns per     step. Uses adaptive stride: window placed     approximately n_pairs / (window_snps*(window_snps-1)/2)     evenly-spaced positions across chromosome, total pairs     stays near n_pairs regardless marker density.     window_snps=50 500k-SNP chromosome     n_pairs=50000: stride=12,195, 41 read_chunk     calls instead 10,000. density guard automatically     switches chromosomes > 200,000 SNPs "random"     sampling (consecutive SNPs WGS density always near-     perfect LD, making sliding-window curve uninformative).     Matches TASSEL approach (Bradbury et al. 2007); recommended     chip-density panels (< 200k SNPs per chromosome). "random" Randomly samples n_pairs SNP pairs     per chromosome within max_dist bp, loads unique     SNPs involved. Bounded RAM regardless panel density; recommended     WGS panels (> 500k SNPs per chromosome). "" Sliding window decay curve shape;     random sampling parametric threshold estimation. Critical r\(^2\) threshold: Fixed numeric (e.g. 0.1) Standard value used GWAS     papers. distance decay curve crosses value defines     LD block extent candidate gene searches. "parametric" 95th percentile r\(^2\) markers     different chromosomes (unlinked markers). structured     population, unlinked r\(^2\) > 0 due kinship. threshold     captures background LD attributable structure, LD     genuine. high parametric threshold (> 0.05) strong indicator     method = "rV2" used block detection. "" Returns ; uses parametric active     threshold decay distance estimation. Decay model: Hill-Weir (1988) expectation relates expected r\(^2\) distance \(d\) (Mb) via \(C = 4 N_e r d\). HapBlockR fits per chromosome C free parameter via nonlinear least squares. LOESS smooth non-parametric alternative robust non-standard decay shapes. Connection define_qtl_regions() GWAS integration: output compute_ld_decay() can passed directly define_qtl_regions(ld_decay = decay) replace fixed block boundaries chromosome-specific LD-aware windows. Without ld_decay define_qtl_regions() asks     blocks CONTAIN significant GWAS SNP? search     window equals block boundary. GWAS hits gaps blocks     near block edges missed. ld_decay Asks blocks LD     significant GWAS SNP? search window extended     chromosome-specific decay distance sides. Adds columns     candidate_region_start, candidate_region_end,     candidate_region_size_kb ready BioMart/Ensembl     Plants candidate gene queries. directly feeds integrate_gwas_haplotypes(): GWAS biological-evidence layer (layer 1 three-evidence score) awards point blocks contain GWAS hit. ld_decay, blocks near hit (within decay distance) also receive evidence point, making three-evidence scoring rank_haplotype_blocks() sensitive biologically accurate. recommended workflow therefore: decay <- compute_ld_decay(, ...) qtl <- define_qtl_regions(..., ld_decay = decay) ranked <- integrate_gwas_haplotypes(qtl, pred, ...)

what: Compute Local Haplotype GEBV per Block (Tong et al. 2025) — compute_local_gebv
title: Compute Local Haplotype GEBV per Block (Tong et al. 2025) — compute_local_gebv
text: LD block, computes local GEBV (haplotype effect) every individual summing per-SNP additive effects alleles carry within block: $$\text{local GEBV}_f = \sum_{t \f} (x_t - 2 p_t)\,\alpha_t$$ \(x_t\) allele dosage (0/1/2) SNP \(t\), \(p_t\) SNP's population allele frequency, \(\alpha_t\) additive effect. Centring \(2p_t\) (rather heterozygote midpoint, dosage = 1) matches convention used backsolve_snp_effects derive alpha first place (\(\text{GEBV} = M\alpha\) \(M\) centred \(2p\)), summing local_gebv across every block one individual reconstructs individual's overall backsolved GEBV. Blocks ranked Var(local GEBV) – blocks high variance contribute strongly trait differences among individuals likely harbour causal loci (Tong et al. 2025). ranking unaffected choice centring point (variance shift-invariant), absolute local_gebv values meaningful – .e. summable back genome-wide GEBV – \(2p_t\) convention used .

what: When to use r^2 vs rV^2
title: Compute Standard r^2 LD Matrix — compute_r2
text: r^2 Use large unstructured datasets (> 500 k markers), random     mating populations, whenever speed matters. standard estimator     inflated related populations (.e. -estimate LD)     usually leads slightly conservative (larger) blocks rather     catastrophically wrong ones. rV^2 Use highly structured / related populations (livestock,     inbred lines, family-based human cohorts) kinship inflation     meaningfully distort block boundaries. Requires computing     inverting GRM - prohibitive beyond ~5 k individuals.

what: Estimate Diplotype Effects and Dominance Deviations Per LD Block — estimate_diplotype_effects
title: Estimate Diplotype Effects and Dominance Deviations Per LD Block — estimate_diplotype_effects
text: Fits per-block diplotype model decompose phenotypic variation additive dominance components LD block, correcting population structure kinship via haplotype GRM. function provides direct evidence non-additive gene action: dominance, overdominance, heterosis. Method: LD block, unique diplotypes (canonical haplotype-pair strings inferred infer_block_haplotypes, e.g. "010/110") treated levels fixed factor. mixed model haplotype GRM kinship random effect fitted via rrBLUP::mixed.solve() obtain de-regressed phenotype residuals. Diplotype class means computed residuals. pair common alleles (, B), classical quantitative genetics parameters derived three diplotype class means: Additive effect: \(= (\bar{y}_{BB} - \bar{y}_{AA}) / 2\) Dominance deviation: \(d = \bar{y}_{AB} -     (\bar{y}_{AA} + \bar{y}_{BB}) / 2\) Dominance ratio: \(d/\) - key quantity interpreting     gene action (see d_over_a column description).

title: Estimate Diplotype Effects and Dominance Deviations Per LD Block — estimate_diplotype_effects
text: haplotypes Named list produced extract_haplotypes. Phase-ambiguous diplotypes (unphased heterozygotes) excluded dominance analysis included omnibus F-test diplotype string unambiguous. accurate dominance decomposition, phased input (read_phased_vcf, phase_with_beagle, via phase_with_beagle) strongly recommended. blues Pre-adjusted phenotype means. Accepts four formats test_block_haplotypes: named numeric vector, single-trait data frame, multi-trait data frame, named list. formats require individual IDs matching names haplotype strings. blocks LD block table run_Big_LD_all_chr. Used supply block coordinate metadata (CHR, start_bp, end_bp) output tables. min_freq Numeric (0, 1). Minimum allele frequency. Alleles threshold full panel excluded dominance decomposition (dominance_table) diplotypes still contribute diplotype_means omnibus_tests sufficient individuals carry . Default 0.05. min_n_diplotype Integer. Minimum number individuals must carry given diplotype class included diplotype_means dominance decomposition. Diplotype classes fewer individuals silently excluded. omnibus F-test uses retained classes. Default 3L. Increasing 5-10 improves mean estimate stability small panels; decreasing 3 recommended. id_col Character. Name individual-ID column blues data frame. Default "id". blue_col Character. Name phenotype column single-trait data frames. Default "blue". blue_cols Character vector. Phenotype column names multi-trait data frames. Default NULL. sig_threshold Numeric (0, 1]. Significance cutoff applied p-value chosen sig_metric. Default 0.05. sig_metric Character. p-value drives significant flag $omnibus_tests. One : "p_omnibus_adj" (default) - plain Bonferroni:     \(\min(p \times n_{blocks},\,1)\), computed per trait.     Retained backward compatibility. "p_omnibus_fdr" - Benjamini-Hochberg FDR per trait. "p_omnibus_simplem" - simpleM Bonferroni-style:     \(\min(p \times M_{\mathrm{eff}},\,1)\),     \(M_{\mathrm{eff}}\) estimated eigenspectrum     block-summary PC1 matrix. "p_omnibus_simplem_sidak" - simpleM Sidak-style:     \(1-(1-p)^{M_{\mathrm{eff}}}\). Recommended: consistent     test_block_haplotypes. four p-value columns always present $omnibus_tests regardless choice. meff_percent_cut Numeric (0, 1). Proportion variance explained retained PCs simpleM eigendecomposition used estimate \(M_{\mathrm{eff}}\) sig_metric = "p_omnibus_simplem" "p_omnibus_simplem_sidak". Default 0.995 (99.5%), following original simpleM recommendation (Gao et al. 2008). meff_max_cols Integer. Maximum columns per eigendecomposition chunk estimating \(M_{\mathrm{eff}}\). Default 1000L. verbose Logical. TRUE (default) prints progress per trait.

title: Estimate Diplotype Effects and Dominance Deviations Per LD Block — estimate_diplotype_effects
text: named list class c("HapBlockR_diplotype", "list")   three elements: diplotype_means Data frame. One row per diplotype class per     LD block per trait, diplotype classes >= min_n_diplotype     individuals. Contains 9 columns: block_id (character) - Block identifier. CHR (character) - Chromosome. start_bp, end_bp (integer) - Block coordinates. trait (character) - Trait name. diplotype (character) - Canonical diplotype string: two         haplotype allele strings sorted alphabetically joined         "/", e.g. "010/110". Homozygotes identical         halves: "010/010". format ensures "010/110"         "110/010" always represented identically. n_class (integer) - Number individuals carrying         specific diplotype combination. n_total (integer) - Total individuals non-missing         data block (sum n_class across diplotype classes). mean_blue (numeric) - Mean de-regressed phenotype value         diplotype class (residual scale GRM correction). se_mean (numeric) - Standard error mean         (sd / sqrt(n_class)). dominance_table Data frame. One row per ordered allele pair     (, B) per block per trait, pairs three diplotype classes     (AA, AB, BB) >= min_n_diplotype individuals.     Contains 14 columns: block_id, CHR, start_bp, end_bp,         trait - . allele_A, allele_B (character) - two alleles         compared (alphabetically ordered: comes B). mean_AA, mean_AB, mean_BB (numeric) -         Diplotype class means de-regressed phenotype scale. (numeric) - Additive effect:         \((\bar{y}_{BB} - \bar{y}_{AA}) / 2\). Positive means allele B         increases trait value relative . d (numeric) - Dominance deviation:         \(\bar{y}_{AB} - (\bar{y}_{AA} + \bar{y}_{BB}) / 2\).         Positive: heterozygote advantage (overdominance \(|d| > ||\)).         Negative: heterozygote disadvantage (underdominance). d_over_a (numeric NA) - Dominance ratio         \(d/\). Interpretation: 0 = purely additive gene action;         \(\pm 0.5\) = partial dominance; \(\pm 1\) = complete dominance         (heterozygote equal one homozygote); \(|d/| > 1\) = overdominance         (heterozygote exceeds homozygotes - evidence heterosis         locus). NA \(|| < 10^{-10}\) (additive         variation homozygotes). overdominance (logical) - TRUE         \(|d/| > 1\) d_over_a NA. omnibus_tests Data frame. One row per LD block per trait,     blocks least min_n_diplotype individuals carry     least 2 distinct diplotype classes. Contains 9 columns: block_id, trait - . n_diplotypes (integer) - Number diplotype classes         >= min_n_diplotype individuals, used factor levels. F_stat (numeric) - F-statistic one-way ANOVA         (diplotype factor) de-regressed phenotype residuals. df1 (integer) - Numerator df = n_diplotypes - 1. df2 (integer) - Denominator df = n_obs - n_diplotypes. p_omnibus (numeric, (0,1]) - Raw p-value. p_omnibus_adj (numeric, (0,1]) - Bonferroni-adjusted         across tested blocks per trait. significant (logical) - TRUE         p_omnibus_adj < 0.05. Sorted ascending p_omnibus.

what: Estimate Per-SNP Marker Effects via GBLUP, rrBLUP (SNP-BLUP), or Bayesian Regression — estimate_marker_effects
title: Estimate Per-SNP Marker Effects via GBLUP, rrBLUP (SNP-BLUP), or Bayesian Regression — estimate_marker_effects
text: Unified "Step B" marker-effect estimator haplotype-stacking pipeline (see run_haplotype_prediction), mirroring flexibility HapSelect's create_marker_effects_file() offers (rrBLUP / BGLR / Sommer / ASReml-R – "model returns vector marker effects aligned map"). Returns named vector per-SNP additive effects centred-dosage (\(2p\)) scale used throughout HapBlockR, ready compute_local_gebv. "gblup" (default) Fits rrBLUP::kin.blup()     supplied genomic/haplotype relationship matrix G,     backsolves per-SNP effects resulting GEBV via     backsolve_snp_effects (VanRaden 2008; Tong et al. 2025),     using every individual present geno_matrix/G.     computation run_haplotype_prediction always     used internally, except function's bespoke "gblup" code path     restricts backsolving phenotyped subset backward     compatibility; calling estimate_marker_effects(method = "gblup")     directly backsolves full population instead. Requires     G. "rrblup" Fits rrBLUP::mixed.solve() directly     marker-effect (SNP-BLUP / ridge-regression BLUP) model,     \(y = \mu + Zu + e\) \(u \sim N(0, \sigma_u^2 )\)     (Meuwissen et al. 2001; Endelman 2011), returning u directly –     relationship matrix backsolving step needed. standard     equal-per-SNP-variance assumption mathematically equivalent     VanRaden GBLUP--backsolve, computed way around. "bayesb", "bayesc", "bayesa" Fit     BGLR::BGLR() corresponding variable-selection prior     (Perez & de los Campos 2014) directly genotype matrix, taking     posterior mean marker effects alpha. "bayesa"     BayesA (marker-specific variances scaled-inverse-chi-squared     prior, point mass zero); "bayesb"/"bayesc" add     point mass zero (variable selection). Note     "bayesr" option: BGLR implement four-component     mixture "BayesR" method (Erbe et al. 2012) – earlier version     function incorrectly assumed , fails runtime     BGLR::BGLR()'s "model BayesR implemented" error;     caught running test suite "bayesr" replaced     real BGLR model "bayesa". Requires BGLR     package (Suggests). BGLR runs MCMC sampler writes     temporary diagnostic files (removed automatically unless     bglr_dir supplied); markedly slower     "gblup"/"rrblup" , stochastic, exactly     reproducible seed set. four methods return gebv scale (\(\hat g = M \hat\alpha\), centred genotype matrix times estimated marker effects), results directly comparable across method choices – e.g. sanity-check one method's block ranking another's.

what: Fine-Map Epistatic SNP Pairs Within a Single Block — fine_map_epistasis_block
title: Fine-Map Epistatic SNP Pairs Within a Single Block — fine_map_epistasis_block
text: Exhaustively adaptively identifies specific SNP pairs within single LD block drive block-level epistatic signal. Three methods available: "pairwise" Exhaustive C(p,2) scan. Tests pairs using     model scan_block_epistasis. Recommended     blocks p <= 200 SNPs. "lasso" Fits LASSO model main effects     pairwise interaction terms using glmnet. Identifies     interaction terms non-zero coefficients cross-validated     lambda. Recommended blocks p > 200 SNPs. "auto" Dispatches "pairwise" p <= 200,     "lasso" otherwise.

what: Fit a Multivariate Genomic BLUP — fit_multitrait_gblup
title: Fit a Multivariate Genomic BLUP — fit_multitrait_gblup
text: Fits multivariate GBLUP restricted maximum likelihood. Without full sampling covariance, model uses \(V = Sigma_g \otimes K + Sigma_e \otimes R\), \(R\) carries relative precision. full sampling covariance \(S\), default \(V = Sigma_g \otimes K + S\); explicit option adds \(Sigma_e \otimes \). what: HapBlockR: Genome-Wide LD Block Detection, Haplotype Analysis, Genomic Prediction, and Breeding Decision Support — HapBlockR-package
title: HapBlockR: Genome-Wide LD Block Detection, Haplotype Analysis, Genomic Prediction, and Breeding Decision Support — HapBlockR-package
text: Fast, scalable linkage disequilibrium (LD) block detection genome-wide SNP data using C++/Armadillo computational core two LD metrics: standard r^2 kinship-adjusted rV^2. Includes haplotype reconstruction, diversity metrics, prediction feature matrices, multi-format genotype /O, downstream breeding-decision layer (optimal contribution selection, genomic mating usefulness criterion, Pareto/core-collection parent-set selection).

title: HapBlockR: Genome-Wide LD Block Detection, Haplotype Analysis, Genomic Prediction, and Breeding Decision Support — HapBlockR-package
text: r^2 (method = "r2") Standard squared Pearson correlation.     kinship matrix required. C++ kernel via RcppArmadillo + OpenMP.     Suitable unstructured populations large datasets (10 M+ markers). rV^2 (method = "rV2") Kinship-whitened squared correlation     (Mangin et al. 2012, Heredity 108:285-291). Corrects LD inflation relatedness. livestock,     inbred lines, family-based cohorts < 200 k markers per chromosome.

title: HapBlockR: Genome-Wide LD Block Detection, Haplotype Analysis, Genomic Prediction, and Breeding Decision Support — HapBlockR-package
text: Read genotype data: read_geno – auto-detects CSV,     HapMap, VCF, GDS, BED, plain matrix. WGS panels peak RAM     concern, use read_geno_bigmemory build     memory-mapped store (requires bigmemory). Detect LD blocks chromosome-wise: run_Big_LD_all_chr. Optionally auto-tune parameters: tune_LD_params. Reconstruct haplotypes: extract_haplotypes. Decode haplotype strings nucleotides:     decode_haplotype_strings. Compute diversity metrics: compute_haplotype_diversity. Build prediction feature matrix:     build_haplotype_feature_matrix. Compute LD decay chromosome-specific decay distances:     compute_ld_decay. Provides critical r\(^2\)     threshold (parametric: 95th percentile unlinked-marker r\(^2\))     per-chromosome decay distances candidate gene windows. Map GWAS hits QTL regions (LD-aware windows     ld_decay supplied): define_qtl_regions. Genomic prediction (Tong et al. 2024/2025):     run_haplotype_prediction – full pipeline BLUEs     block importance; step--step via     compute_haplotype_grm,     backsolve_snp_effects,     compute_local_gebv,     rank_haplotype_blocks. Haplotype association testing simpleM correction     (Gao et al. 2008, 2010, 2011): test_block_haplotypes.     sig_metric selects among p_wald, p_fdr,     p_simplem (Bonferroni-style), p_simplem_sidak     (Sidak-style, recommended). four p-value columns always present.     meff_scope controls Meff estimation scope. Cross-population GWAS validation - two functions depending     association analysis performed: compare_block_effects - results         test_block_haplotypes. IVW meta-analysis, Cochran Q,         -squared, direction agreement per block. compare_gwas_effects - results external         GWAS tools (GAPIT, TASSEL, FarmCPU, PLINK, etc.). Accepts raw GWAS         data frames define_qtl_regions output. Derives SE         z-score absent. functions support block_match = "position" match         LD blocks genomic interval overlap (Intersection--Union) rather         block_id string equality. handles common case         block boundaries differ populations due different         ancestral LD structures. overlap_min (default 0.50) sets         minimum IoU valid positional match. match_type output         column reports "exact", "position",         "pop1_only" every block. Write outputs: write_haplotype_numeric,     write_haplotype_character,     write_haplotype_diversity. run everything : run_ldx_pipeline.

what: Harmonise Haplotype Allele Labels Across Panels or Analysis Runs — harmonize_haplotypes
title: Harmonise Haplotype Allele Labels Across Panels or Analysis Runs — harmonize_haplotypes
text: Ensures haplotype allele labels biologically comparable across different datasets, analysis runs, training/validation splits. Without harmonization, allele string "010110" one panel guaranteed correspond biological haplotype another panel block boundaries, SNP ordering, allele encoding differ runs. function anchors allele identity reference dictionary built training/reference panel. New (target) haplotypes matched dictionary: Exact match: allele string exists verbatim     reference dictionary -> labelled reference allele label. Nearest-Hamming match: exact match -> labelled     similar reference allele (minimum Hamming distance).     minimum Hamming distance exceeds max_hamming, allele     labelled "<novel>". Novel: distance > max_hamming -> "<novel>".

Cross-population effect concordance from external GWAS results. # Here ldx_gwas is used for both populations; in practice these # would be independent GWAS runs on separate cohorts. set.seed(1L) gwas_pop2        <- ldx_gwas gwas_pop2$BETA   <- ldx_gwas$BETA * 0.8 + rnorm(20, 0, 0.02) gwas_pop2$SE     <- ldx_gwas$SE   * 0.9 + runif(20, 0, 0.005) gwas_pop2$P      <- 2 * pnorm(-abs(gwas_pop2$BETA / gwas_pop2$SE))  # Path 1: pre-mapped (recommended for auditability) qtl1 <- define_qtl_regions(ldx_gwas,  ldx_blocks, ldx_snp_info,                            p_threshold = NULL, verbose = FALSE) qtl2 <- define_qtl_regions(gwas_pop2, ldx_blocks, ldx_snp_info,                            p_threshold = NULL, verbose = FALSE) conc <- compare_gwas_effects(   qtl_pop1    = qtl1,   qtl_pop2    = qtl2,   blocks_pop1 = ldx_blocks,   blocks_pop2 = ldx_blocks,   pop1_name   = "DiscoveryPop",   pop2_name   = "ReplicationPop",   verbose     = FALSE ) conc$concordance[, c("block_id","direction_agreement","meta_p","replicated")] #>                block_id direction_agreement       meta_p replicated #> 1    block_1_1000_25027                   1 1.855521e-10       TRUE #> 2   block_1_81064_99022                   1 1.687084e-11       TRUE #> 3 block_1_155368_179371                   1 3.037882e-14       TRUE #> 4    block_2_1000_30023                   1 1.409021e-07       TRUE #> 5  block_2_86236_105290                   1 3.304721e-07       TRUE #> 6    block_3_1000_19068                   1 7.263598e-03       TRUE  # Path 2: raw GWAS + blocks (calls define_qtl_regions internally) conc2 <- compare_gwas_effects(   gwas_pop1     = ldx_gwas,   gwas_pop2     = gwas_pop2,   blocks_pop1   = ldx_blocks,   blocks_pop2   = ldx_blocks,   snp_info_pop1 = ldx_snp_info,   p_threshold   = NULL,   verbose       = FALSE ) print(conc2) #> HapBlockR Cross-Population Effect Concordance #>   Populations: pop1 vs pop2 #>   Traits:       trait  #>   Blocks compared:           6  #>   With enough shared alleles: 6  #>   Directionally concordant:   6  #>   Replicated (dir + Q_p>0.05): 6  #>   Boundary warnings:          0 (overlap ratio < 0.8 ) #>   Shared allele comparisons:  6  # }

title: Pareto (Non-Dominated) Front of a Set of Candidates — pareto_front
text: Uses standard \(O(n^2 \times k)\) pairwise-dominance algorithm (\(n\) = candidates, \(k\) = objectives) – exact, heuristic, intended huge candidate sets (low hundreds comfortable; thousands slow). Among non-dominated set, also computes NSGA-II crowding distance (Deb et al. 2002) per objective secondary diagnostic: candidates near extremes front get Inf; candidates sparsely populated regions front get larger value candidates crowded next near-identical alternatives. purely descriptive (non-dominated points "distinct" neighbours front) – change points Pareto-optimal.

title: Haplotype Prediction and Block Importance from Pre-Adjusted Phenotypes — run_haplotype_prediction
text: geno_matrix Numeric matrix (individuals x SNPs), values 0/1/2/NA. Row names must genotype IDs. snp_info Data frame columns SNP, CHR, POS. blocks Block table run_Big_LD_all_chr. blues Pre-adjusted phenotype values. See section accepted formats. id_col Name ID column blues data frame. Default "id". blue_col Name BLUE column single-trait data frames. Default "blue". blue_cols Character vector trait column names multi-trait data frames. Default NULL – numeric non-ID columns used. importance_rule set combined important flag multi-trait results: "" (default): TRUE important >= 1 trait. "": TRUE important traits. "mean": TRUE var_scaled_mean >= 0.9. Ignored single-trait runs (single-trait important always scaled variance >= 0.9). top_n Integer NULL. Max haplotype alleles per block. Default NULL. min_freq Minimum haplotype allele frequency. Default 0.01. min_snps Minimum SNPs per block. Default 3L. affects haplotype feature matrix used GRM/diversity (hap_matrix, haplotypes); local GEBV decomposition governed separately complete_decomposition. bend Logical. Add ridge GRM diagonal. Default TRUE. marker_effect_method One "gblup" (default), "rrblup", "bayesb", "bayesc", "bayesa". See Marker-effect estimation methods section. include_dominance Logical, default FALSE. Fit joint additive + dominance model instead additive-. valid marker_effect_method = "gblup"; requires BGLR. See Additive + dominance GBLUP section. complete_decomposition Logical. Default TRUE. Passed compute_local_gebv: guarantees every SNP known effect attributed block (singleton pseudo-block covered blocks), rowSums(local_gebv) reconstructs individual's full backsolved GEBV – matching HapSelect's completeness guarantee localGEBV. Set FALSE restore previous behaviour (SNPs outside every block window dropped). importance_threshold Numeric (0,1]. Scaled-variance cutoff important flag (single-trait, multi-trait importance_rule = "mean"). Default 0.9 (unchanged previous releases). See also select_top_blocks count/percentage/cumulative-variance selection instead fixed cutoff. n_iter, burn_in Integer. MCMC iterations / burn-, used marker_effect_method "bayesb"/"bayesc"/"bayesa". Defaults 6000/1000. seed Integer NULL. Random seed Bayesian methods (ignored otherwise). Default NULL. min_reliability Numeric [0, 1]. Minimum GEBV reliability individual marked recommendable gebv_uncertainty. Default 0.30. Methods expose prediction error variance return missing reliability promoted recommendations. verbose Logical. Print progress. Default TRUE. ploidy Integer >= 2. Ploidy level geno_matrix's dosage encoding. Default 2L (diploid, unchanged previous releases). Passed backsolve_snp_effects/ estimate_marker_effects/compute_local_gebv marker effects local GEBVs use ploidy-generalised VanRaden centring (\(\text{ploidy} \cdot p\) instead \(2p\)). affect shared GRM (G), always built haplotype-allele feature matrix – derived HapBlockR's diploid-hap1/hap2 phased representation, dosage columns always 0/1/2 regardless argument. Set geno_matrix holds raw 0..ploidy dosage calls higher-ploidy species.

title: Haplotype Prediction and Block Importance from Pre-Adjusted Phenotypes — run_haplotype_prediction
text: traits fitted using rrBLUP::kin.blup() per-trait loop sharing GRM. produces numerically identical results sommer::mmes() single-trait models (verified empirically 4 decimal places), avoiding multi-trait cbind() formula fails sommer <= 4.4.5 (Armadillo fixed-size matrix error C++ coefficient matrix construction). traits use GRM, cross-trait block importance values directly comparable. solver_used "rrBLUP" default marker_effect_method = "gblup"; see next section methods.

title: Haplotype Prediction and Block Importance from Pre-Adjusted Phenotypes — run_haplotype_prediction
text: marker_effect_method selects "Step B" pipeline – per-SNP effects derived summing within block (Step C). four options ultimately call estimate_marker_effects produce snp_effects vector centred-dosage scale, local_gebv/block_importance comparable across methods: "gblup" (default) rrBLUP::kin.blup()     haplotype-block GRM, backsolved per-SNP effects     (backsolve_snp_effects; VanRaden 2008; Tong et al. 2025).     method pipeline always used. "rrblup" rrBLUP::mixed.solve() fit directly     marker-effect (SNP-BLUP / ridge-regression) model – relationship     matrix backsolving step (Meuwissen et al. 2001; Endelman 2011). "bayesb", "bayesc", "bayesa" Bayesian     variable-selection regression via BGLR::BGLR() (Perez & de los     Campos 2014). Requires BGLR package. Slower (MCMC)     stochastic unless seed set. ("bayesr" option –     BGLR implement four-component-mixture "BayesR" method;     see estimate_marker_effects's documentation.) Mirrors flexibility HapSelect's create_marker_effects_file() (rrBLUP / BGLR / Sommer / ASReml-R).

text: default (include_dominance = FALSE), pipeline – like estimate_marker_effects – additive-. Set include_dominance = TRUE (marker_effect_method = "gblup") fit joint additive + dominance model instead: compute_dominance_grm builds dominance relationship matrix \(G_D\) (Vitezica, Varona & Legarra 2013) raw SNP dosage matrix, paired existing haplotype-block additive GRM \(G_A\) two random-effect kernels single BGLR::BGLR(ETA = list(list(K = G_A, model = "RKHS"), list(K = G_D, model = "RKHS"))) call – rrBLUP::kin.blup() (default GBLUP solver) accepts single relationship matrix partition additive/dominance variance. Relevant trait suspected heterosis/overdominance, estimate_diplotype_effects can already flag per block via d/ratio. Requires BGLR package. Adds dominance_deviation, total_genetic_value (gebv + dominance_deviation), G_dominance return value (NULL include_dominance = FALSE, return list's field names stable regardless argument). Scope limit: per-SNP/per-block decomposition (snp_effects, local_gebv, block_importance) remains additive-even include_dominance = TRUE – backsolve_snp_effects additive-formula, block-level dominance decomposition settled methodology (see compute_dominance_grm's documentation).

what: Finlay-Wilkinson Stability Analysis of Haplotype Effects Across Environments — run_haplotype_stability
title: Finlay-Wilkinson Stability Analysis of Haplotype Effects Across Environments — run_haplotype_stability
text: Estimates stability haplotype block's effect across multiple environments using Finlay-Wilkinson (1963) regression. block, per-environment GEBV contribution regressed environment mean (environmental index). regression slope b_i = 1 indicates average stability; b_i > 1 = -average response (exploits good environments); b_i < 1 = -average response (robust across environments).

what: Between-Block Haplotype Allele Epistasis Scan — scan_block_by_block_epistasis
title: Between-Block Haplotype Allele Epistasis Scan — scan_block_by_block_epistasis
text: Tests interactions haplotype allele dosage columns different LD blocks. significant allele (test_block_haplotypes), tests interaction every haplotype allele blocks: $$y = \mu + \alpha_i x_i + \alpha_j x_j + \gamma_{ij}(x_i x_j) + \varepsilon$$ Restricting significant alleles x blocks gives O(n_sig x n_total_alleles) tests – tractable WGS scale. panel: ~25 significant alleles x 17,943 alleles = ~450,000 tests. trans-haplotype epistasis scan: tests whether effect resistance haplotype one block depends haplotype background another block – form genetic background dependence single-SNP even single-block analyses detect.

what: Within-Block Pairwise SNP Epistasis Scan — scan_block_epistasis
title: Within-Block Pairwise SNP Epistasis Scan — scan_block_epistasis
text: Tests pairwise SNP x SNP interactions within haplotype blocks identified significant test_block_haplotypes. significant block, C(p, 2) SNP pairs tested interaction using model: $$y = \mu + a_i x_i + a_j x_j + aa_{ij}(x_i x_j) + \varepsilon$$ GRM-corrected REML residuals (null model test_block_haplotypes), ensuring tests population-structure-corrected. Restricting significant blocks avoids genome-wide explosion pairwise tests: 15 significant blocks ~200 SNPs , total number tests ~300,000, compared ~4.4 billion unrestricted genome-wide scan.

what: Score Individual Haplotype Portfolios Against Known Allele Effects — score_favorable_haplotypes
title: Score Individual Haplotype Portfolios Against Known Allele Effects — score_favorable_haplotypes
text: Scores individual's genome-wide haplotype composition table per-allele effects (genomic prediction association analysis), producing per-block score genome-wide stacking index. primary tool translating haplotype genomic prediction results actionable breeding rankings. Scoring rule: individual \(\) LD block \(b\), block score : $$s_{ib} = \sum_{j} \hat{\alpha}_j \cdot d_{ij}$$ \(\hat{\alpha}_j\) known effect allele \(j\) \(d_{ij}\) dosage (copies) allele \(j\) carried individual \(\) (0/1 unphased data; 0/1/2 phased data). genome-wide stacking index sum block scores across scored blocks, optionally normalised [0, 1].

title: Core-Collection / Diversity-Maximizing Subset Selection — select_core_collection
text: "maximin" (Default.) Farthest-point traversal (Gonzalez     1985): start single genetically distant pair,     repeatedly add whichever remaining candidate largest MINIMUM     distance everything already selected. Maximizes smallest     pairwise distance final set (guards near-duplicate     individuals slipping ), proven 2-approximation guarantee.     standard "M strategy" core-collection literature. "mean_distance" step, adds whichever remaining     candidate increases selected set's MEAN pairwise distance     ("MD strategy"). Tends spread selection evenly across     whole diversity space rather prioritising single     extreme outliers; expensive compute (recomputed per candidate     per step) still tractable typical core-collection sizes. Neither exact solver objective (standard greedy heuristics used throughout core-collection literature, guaranteed-optimal search) – see validate_crosses_exact need true optimum small-enough problem (function targets cross selection specifically, subset-diversity problem, shares "exact validation heuristic" philosophy).

title: Block-Level Haplotype Association Testing (Q+K Mixed Linear Model with simpleM Multiple-Testing Correction) — test_block_haplotypes
text: Performs genome-wide haplotype block association tests one quantitative traits. LD block tested unit: per-allele Wald tests identify specific haplotype alleles drive association, omnibus F-test evaluates block whole. Population structure kinship corrected jointly unified mixed linear model. addition raw FDR-adjusted p-values, function applies simpleM-style multiple-testing correction account correlation among tested haplotype alleles. simpleM estimates effective number independent tests (\(M_{\mathrm{eff}}\)) eigenvalues haplotype allele correlation matrix derives either Bonferroni-style Sidak-style adjusted threshold. Statistical model (Q+K / EMMAX formulation): $$y = \mu + \alpha \cdot x_{\mathrm{hap}} +        \sum_{k=1}^{K} \beta_k \, PC_k + g + \varepsilon$$ \(x_{\mathrm{hap}}\) Haplotype allele dosage (0, 1, 2 copies     phased data; 0 1 unphased). \(PC_k\) k-th eigenvector haplotype GRM,     fixed-effect covariate population structure. \(g \sim MVN(0,\,\sigma_g^2 G)\) Polygenic background     random effect. \(\varepsilon \sim MVN(0,\,\sigma_e^2 )\) Residual error. null model (\(\sigma_g^2\), \(\sigma_e^2\)) fit per trait via rrBLUP::mixed.solve() (REML). marker tested true GLS/EMMAX transform: phenotype every haplotype-allele column pre-multiplied \(\hat V^{-1/2}\), \(\hat V = \hat\sigma_g^2 G + \hat\sigma_e^2 \), via null model's GRM eigendecomposition (computed per trait reused every marker), transformed null design (intercept + PCs) projected via Frisch-Waugh-Lovell theorem per-allele per-block tests. mathematically equivalent full per-marker GLS fit \(\hat V\), approximation. null-model fit, GRM eigendecomposition, transformed null-design inversion fails, function falls back faster residual-scan approximation (subtracting estimated fixed effects polygenic BLUP, OLS remains) emits warning identifying affected trait. simpleM extension (Gao et al. 2008, 2010, 2011): \(M_{\mathrm{eff}}\) estimated eigenspectrum haplotype allele dosage correlation matrix - number principal components needed explain meff_percent_cut variance (default 99.5%). Two simpleM adjusted p-value paths always computed: p_simplem - Bonferroni-style:     \(\min(p \times M_{\mathrm{eff}},\,1)\). p_simplem_sidak - Sidak-style:     \(1 - (1 - p)^{M_{\mathrm{eff}}}\). haplotype alleles correlated within across nearby blocks, simpleM less conservative raw Bonferroni still providing family-wise error control.

text: classical UC formula assumes infinite, normally-distributed progeny population. Real biparental crosses produce tens hundred progeny, TRUE expected selection intensity finite sample somewhat smaller asymptotic formula gives (order-statistics theory: expected mean top k n draws converges , equal, top-p-quantile density ratio n grows). Supplying n_progeny switches Monte Carlo estimate exact finite-sample intensity (see n_sim, seed) rather approximate closed-form small-sample correction – deliberately, since several closed-form corrections exist literature mutually consistent, whereas finite-sample order-statistic mean estimable directly exactly (Monte Carlo error) simulation. Leave n_progeny = NULL use standard asymptotic formula (fine large planned progeny numbers, pre-existing default behaviour). variance modes, predicted_variance reflects segregation target blocks block_importance , whole genome – tractability trade-select_parents_ga makes pre-filtering manageable set top-ranked blocks. block_importance covers blocks explaining local-GEBV variance (e.g. via select_top_blocks), captures segregating variance matters practice, exactly whole-genome quantity classical UC formulations assume. mid_parent_gebv (mean term), contrast, always uses full whole-genome gebv supply, since best available estimate cross's mean.

Responses converted engine’s analysis scale original trait units, including scaling requested, selection intensity reflects number actually selected. qgsi_control exposes non-structural run_qgsi() controls without allowing HapBlockR’s data, objective, direction selection-count arguments overridden. Integration tests now compare delegated outputs directly updated DesiredGainR engines, including reference scaling, holdout selection, eligibility thresholds, explicit genomic covariance relationship-aware covariance estimation. Control names must match installed API exactly. DGSI returns coefficients_original_units score_intercept correct original-unit effect propagation score reconstruction, preserving engine’s coefficients complete result. Result provenance records dependency version hashes objective engine controls. Multivariate GxE REML likelihoods now use residual degrees freedom. Full sampling covariance uses exact target record keys checked diagonal precision. sampling_covariance_mode explicitly selects sampling-sampling-plus-residual models, preventing silent covariance loss unintended residual duplication. sampling-optimiser longer allocates dense zero matrix every objective evaluation. GxE across-environment predictions select one row explicitly per genotype, avoiding BLAS-dependent duplicate IDs caused final-decimal differences. Kernel diagonal validation independent spectral PSD tolerance, selection intensity requires one positive finite real scalar.
